title: Revenue as a Function of Price
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: A vendor faces the demand law $q=100-2p$, where $p$ is the unit price in dollars and $q$ the quantity sold. Write revenue $R$ as a function of $p$ and give the economically sensible domain.

steps.title: Apply the Revenue Identity
steps.explanation: Revenue is total money taken in, the product of per-unit price and units sold.
steps.why: The definition $R=pq$ is the bridge from demand to revenue.

steps.title: Substitute the Demand Law
steps.explanation: Replacing $q$ by $100-2p$ turns revenue into a downward-opening quadratic in $p$.
steps.why: Expressing everything in price makes $R$ a single-variable function.

steps.title: Bound the Price
steps.explanation: Prices cannot be negative, and demand $100-2p$ must stay non-negative, which caps the price at $50$.
steps.why: Business models restrict domains by the meaning of their quantities.
